subject.title: feat(linux): Quick Chat agent switcher, avatars, per-agent routing, and configurable shortcut

question: Should Linux Quick Chat accept configured remote avatar URLs by broadening its local webview img-src policy to HTTP(S), or should avatar rendering remain restricted to a narrower trusted source model?
rationale: The branch deliberately changes a webview CSP boundary to render user-configured avatar URLs; source history in the provided context establishes the feature direction but not a maintainer-approved trust policy for arbitrary remote image requests.

options.title: Accept the shared avatar policy
options.body: Confirm that Quick Chat may use the existing avatar resolver's HTTP(S), data URI, and local-file-to-data-URI outputs, then review the rebased implementation and merge with its documented behavior.

options.title: Restrict avatar sources
options.body: Keep Quick Chat avatar rendering to data URIs or an explicitly trusted/proxied source and revise the CLI/UI contract before merging.

recommendation.title: Accept the shared avatar policy
recommendation.body: Confirm that Quick Chat may use the existing avatar resolver's HTTP(S), data URI, and local-file-to-data-URI outputs, then review the rebased implementation and merge with its documented behavior.
